plugin.ecb.title: ECB mode (electronic codebook)
plugin.ecb.preset.repeated-blocks: Two equal plaintext blocks: ECB shows the repetition
plugin.ecb.preset.repeated-blocks-decryp: Decrypt the two-block message and remove its padding
plugin.ecb.param.cipherHint: The block cipher E_K that ECB calls once per block.
plugin.ecb.param.keyHint: A key the block cipher accepts, e.g. 16, 24 or 32 bytes for AES.
plugin.ecb.param.inputHint: Up to 64 bytes: the plaintext to encrypt or the ciphertext to decrypt.
plugin.ecb.param.paddingHint: PKCS#7 fills the last block up; without padding the input must be whole blocks.
plugin.ecb.step.initialEncrypt: The plaintext has {{bytes}} bytes. ECB encrypts it in blocks of {{blockSize}} bytes with {{cipher}}, each block on its own with the same key. Equal plaintext blocks therefore give equal ciphertext blocks.
plugin.ecb.step.initialDecrypt_one: The ciphertext has {{bytes}} bytes in one block. ECB decrypts it on its own with {{cipher}}.
plugin.ecb.step.initialDecrypt_other: The ciphertext has {{bytes}} bytes in {{count}} blocks. ECB decrypts each block on its own with {{cipher}}.
plugin.ecb.step.pad: PKCS#7 padding: {{count}} bytes of value {{byte}} fill the input up to {{length}} bytes, a whole number of blocks. Even an input that already fills its blocks gets a full block of padding, so the receiver can always remove it.
plugin.ecb.step.encryptBlock: Block {{n}}: {{cipher}} encrypts P{{n}} = {{input}} to {{output}}. Here E_K is one opaque step; open the block cipher's lab to see its rounds.
plugin.ecb.step.emitEncrypt: C{{n}} = {{block}} goes out. It depends only on P{{n}} and the key, not on any other block.
plugin.ecb.step.unpad: The last byte is {{byte}}, and the last {{count}} bytes all have that value: the padding is valid. Removing it leaves {{length}} bytes of plaintext.
plugin.ecb.step.unpadInvalid.empty: There is no data, so there is no padding to remove.
plugin.ecb.step.unpadInvalid.not-block-a: The data is not a whole number of blocks, so the padding is invalid.
plugin.ecb.step.unpadInvalid.zero-pad-by: The last byte is 00, but PKCS#7 never pads with zero bytes: the padding is invalid. The output keeps all decrypted blocks.
plugin.ecb.step.unpadInvalid.pad-too-lon: The last byte is {{byte}}, which claims more padding than one block of {{blockSize}} bytes holds: the padding is invalid. The output keeps all decrypted blocks.
plugin.ecb.step.unpadInvalid.inconsisten: The last byte {{byte}} claims that many padding bytes, but byte {{index}} is {{found}}: the padding is invalid. The output keeps all decrypted blocks.
plugin.ecb.error.invalidParams: Give the key and the input as hex text.
plugin.ecb.error.keyLength: The key has {{length}} bytes; it needs 1 to 64.
plugin.ecb.error.inputLength: The input has {{length}} bytes; it needs 1 to 64.
plugin.ecb.error.notAligned: The input has {{length}} bytes, which is not a multiple of the block size {{blockSize}}. Decrypting, or encrypting without padding, needs whole blocks.
